model_organism.citation: Mov10 suppresses retroelements and regulates neuronal development and function in the developing brain (PMID: 28662698)
phenotypes: Homozygous loss of Mov10 caused early embryonic lethality (no knockout mice obtained)
Mov10 heterozygotes showed reduced dendritic arborization in cultured hippocampal neurons
Reduced Mov10 in brain caused anxiety-like behavior
Reduced Mov10 caused increased activity in a novel environment

Mov10 bound retroelement RNAs and cytoskeletal mRNAs in brain

Zygotic Mov10 knockdown caused abnormal head, eye and brain development

biological.citation: Targeting age-related LINE-1 activation alleviates cardiac aging (PMID: 41571992)
biological.summary: Cardiomyocyte-specific Mov10-knockout mice failed to suppress LINE-1. They developed LINE-1 derepression, cGAS-STING activation, cardiac dysfunction and premature cardiac aging by 3 months. Inhibiting LINE-1 reverse transcription (3TC) or STING (H-151) rescued senescence in Mov10-KO H9C2 cells and improved cardiac function in aged mice.

biological.citation: MOV10 Helicase Interacts with Coronavirus Nucleocapsid Protein and Has Antiviral Activity (PMID: 34517762)
biological.summary: MOV10 relocalizes to cytoplasmic structures with the MERS-CoV nucleocapsid (N) protein and co-immunoprecipitates with N. This interaction is conserved across human CoVs, including SARS-CoV-2. MOV10 silencing increased virus titer and N accumulation, while overexpression lowered titers about 10-fold. The antiviral effect required helicase activity (tested in CRISPR MOV10-KO cells) and was seen only with highly pathogenic CoVs. Viral RNAs were found in MOV10 complexes, suggesting RNA sequestration.

biological.citation: MOV10 Provides Antiviral Activity against RNA Viruses by Enhancing RIG-I-MAVS-Independent IFN Induction (PMID: 27016603)
biological.summary: MOV10 is an IFN-inducible helicase with antiviral activity against several RNA viruses that does not depend on helicase function. It enhances IRF3-mediated type I IFN induction through IKKε (not TBK1), independently of the RIG-I/MAVS pathway. Picornaviral proteases target MOV10 for degradation as an immune evasion mechanism. Shown in genome-edited knockout human cells.

biological.citation: FMRP and MOV10 regulate Dicer1 expression and dendrite development (PMID: 34847178)
biological.summary: Reduced MOV10 in neurons and tissues lowers DICER expression, and Dicer1 mRNA is a CLIP target of MOV10, FMRP and AGO2. The MOV10-FMRP-AGO2 complex regulates DICER1 through its 3'UTR. A DICER1 transgene rescued neurite outgrowth in Mov10-KO Neuro2A cells and branching in Mov10 heterozygote neurons.

biological.citation: MOV10 sequesters the RNP of influenza A virus in the cytoplasm and is antagonized by viral NS1 protein (PMID: 30617221)
biological.summary: MOV10 interacts with influenza A nucleoprotein (NP), sequesters viral RNP in the cytoplasm and promotes vRNA degradation. This depends on intact P-bodies. Viral NS1 disrupts the MOV10-NP interaction and drives lysosomal degradation of MOV10.

biological.citation: Perturbation of the P-body component Mov10 inhibits HIV-1 infectivity (PMID: 20140200)
biological.summary: Mov10 is a P-body-associated protein. Overexpression inhibits infectious HIV-1, other lentiviruses and MLV, acting at the pre-reverse transcription stage. siRNA knockdown modestly reduces HIV infectivity. The N-terminal half is required for activity, while helicase mutation or C-terminal truncation largely preserves it.

biological.citation: Biological and RNA regulatory function of MOV10 in mammalian germ cells (PMID: 31088452)
biological.summary: MOV10 is a nucleocytoplasmic protein mainly expressed in spermatogonia. Knockdown impairs spermatogonial progenitor cell proliferation and in vivo repopulation, disturbs RNA homeostasis and impairs miRNA biogenesis. MOV10 binds mRNAs with long 3'UTRs and non-coding RNAs, and nuclear MOV10 associates with splicing factors such as SRSF1.

biological.citation: Mov10 suppresses retroelements and regulates neuronal development and function in the developing brain (PMID: 28662698)
biological.summary: Homozygous Mov10 loss causes early embryonic lethality in mice. Mov10 is elevated in postnatal brain, where it binds retroelement RNAs and cytoskeletal mRNAs. Nuclear Mov10 suppresses retroelements by inhibiting cDNA synthesis. Heterozygotes show reduced dendritic arborization and anxiety-like behavior, and Mov10-KO Neuro2A cells have shortened neurites. Mov10, Fmrp and Ago2 bind a common set of mRNAs.

biological.citation: Interplay between RNASEH2 and MOV10 controls LINE-1 retrotransposition (PMID: 29315404)
biological.summary: Proteomics identified RNASEH2 as a MOV10 binding partner. The two co-localize in the nucleus, and RNASEH2 binds L1 RNA in a MOV10-dependent manner. Depleting either protein causes accumulation of L1 RNA-DNA hybrids and increased L1 retrotransposition. This loss of restriction raises expression of rheumatoid arthritis-associated cytokines and proteinases in synovial cells.

biological.citation: ASHG 2012 - Mapping the L1 interactome reveals RISC-associated helicase MOV10 as a potent inhibitor of retrotransposition
biological.summary: MOV10 was identified in an L1 RNP proteomic screen (IP and MS). It associates with L1 RNP alongside DDX5, DHX9, DDX17, DDX21 and DDX39A. It co-localizes with L1 ORF1p in stress granules and P-bodies. MOV10 strongly restricts L1, Alu and SVA retrotransposition in cell culture, dependent on intact helicase domains, and reduces endogenous and ectopic L1 expression. The other helicases do not strongly inhibit retrotransposition.
